chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim, from 'Ali, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a mouse that falls into a well. He said: seven buckets. He said: And I asked him عليه السلام about a bird and a chicken falling into the well. He said: seven buckets; and for a cat, twenty or thirty or forty buckets; and for a dog and the like of it.

key_terms.الدَّجَاجَةِ: a chicken falling into the well
key_terms.السِّنَّوْرِ: a cat, for which a larger number of buckets is mentioned
key_terms.الطَّيْرِ: a bird falling into the well
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is discussed in purification law
key_terms.الْفَأْرَةِ: a mouse whose fall into the well is asked about
key_terms.الْكَلْبِ: a dog, mentioned with similar impure cases
key_terms.دَلْوًا: a bucket drawn from the well as part of purification
key_terms.سَبْعُ دِلَاءٍ: seven buckets to be drawn from the well

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a mouse, bird, chicken, cat, or dog falling into a well according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings regarding the purification of well water when certain animals fall into it. It specifies the number of buckets to be drawn in different cases, placing the report within the jurisprudence of ritual purity.
